preamble: Debuccalization of the voiced velar fricative [ɣ] to a glottal fricative. Across the Slavic g-spirantization area, *g first became [ɣ] and then moved to the glottis. Czech, Slovak, Ukrainian and Belarusian ended with voiced [ɦ], but Upper Sorbian, where the change is dated to the 14th century, has a voiceless glottal /h/ (hora 'mountain', noha 'leg' < Proto-Slavic *gora, *noga). Lower Sorbian and Polish kept /g/. No well-documented case with a voiceless [h] outcome outside West Slavic has been found, so the change counts as rare.

examples.note: Lower Sorbian keeps góra. The modern phonology lists Upper Sorbian /h/ as a voiceless glottal fricative.
Intervocalic case of the same change; Lower Sorbian has noga.
